title: Roguelite baby needs a tool to grow.
author: Sergiyakun
selftext: Hey all. I have been working on a. Game for weeks. Basically creating a design document but I M curious where I can put a game like this that’d be free for me to start. It’s a rogulite with multiple characters think Suikoden almost with 200 stages and relics etc. where can I go to get a first working build ?

comments.author: _Vultrix_
comments.body: give it to codex or claude code but its gonna be ai slop.

replies.author: Sergiyakun
replies.body: In what way. What would be cheapest then

replies.author: No_Background9234
replies.body: Manually writing your own code, and making you own assets to use would be the cheapest and most effective at getting anyone to play it, otherwise you’re gonna have to spend months and months iterating on it to make it playable and fun

replies.author: _Vultrix_
replies.body: its gonna be ai slop as in your mentality of just giving a gdd to an ai and magically spit out a game means that the game is going to come out as sloppy and low quality. Do you have plan for making assets? animations?

replies.author: Careless_Road8873
replies.body:
Handing a GDD to an AI and waiting for a game won't work. But AI can do most of the typing if you stay the one making the decisions.

I've been making a medieval RPG with a friend this way (SOFT, on itch). Claude writes almost all of the code, around 170k lines in Godot now. The cheap part isn't the code though. It's everything around it:

Small steps. One system at a time, play it, then the next. Never "build the game".

Tests that play the game and take screenshots of every screen, so mistakes get caught before you look at them.

Assets are the hard part. I generate pictures from one style guide and one reference image, throw away most of them, and make the animations from short video clips that a script cuts into frames. That's months of work on its own, so plan for it.

Someone still has to have taste and say no a lot. That part doesn't get cheaper.

So cheapest in money, yes. Cheapest in time, only if you're ready to play your own game every day and be picky.

comments.author: Agile_Branch_8743
comments.body: Start by building 1-2 characters and a stage. Make sure it feels fun. Then add more stuff. You can try with Claude or Codex, but you will need to be specific and do several iterations to get good results.

comments.author: Mrbuttshaman
comments.body:
You are going to want claude sonnet at a minimum\~$20 a month.  You can use it to help you refine your game design document, the story, the dialogue, etc.  I say use claude sonnet because its good enough to help you do the work in small chunks which is all you really need if you aren't making slop.  You are going to have to heavily playtest every element if you want it to be any good.  Also at the start, you want Claude to heavily interrogate you for every design decision.  Its a pain to do but it really is the only way it remains your game and not some thing where the AI made a ton of decisions and you kinda just lightly participated.  It also helps you to set rules for it.  Secondly, you are going to want something like pixellab, or gemini flow to use nano banana 2 to generate character references and sprite sheets which is about another \~$20 a month for either option.  You technically can use nano banana 2 for free in a lot of places but the generations are low or you are risking your data going to some random providers which you might not want to be the case.  Generally, its good to use claude to help you structure your prompts, but its extremely important to create 360 degree character references so the character style doesn't drift.  That's a tell tale symptom of AI generations and if you don't lock it down, everyone will think your game is slop.  The good news is that for audio, sound effects, voice acting, and music, you can get by pretty easily with local models since they don't require a ton of vram for audio ones.  You can download comfy UI, get ace step audio, qwen tts, and stable audio.  That said, you can ask Claude for some of this and it will help you.  You can use tiled to help with generating the map.  [https://thorbjorn.itch.io/tiled](https://thorbjorn.itch.io/tiled)  or you could use pixellab or even nano banana by drawing references and with heavy prompting.  Anyway, you can do almost all of this devoting a crapload of time and for around $50 for a month which is extremely cheap really for what you are able to pull off.

If you have a graphics card with 16GB of vram, you get pretty far with locally generating all of the assets anyway with claude and comfy UI alone if you use claude to develop better tools for communicating with it(like an app or html pages) I know not everyone has that which is why I mentioned the other options first.

comments.author: Here4uman
comments.body: Start slow, build one or 2 steps at a time. Be honest with yourself and work hard to achieve your dream. You can do it. Just make it happen!
